Beyond discrete-time intensive longitudinal models, `DSEMr` provides native
compiled Rust estimators for **Continuous-Time DSEM** (`dsem_ct()`), **random
residual covariances** (`logvf`), exact collapsed **ARMA(1,1)** dynamics,
**cross-classified dynamic factor models with random factor loadings**, and a
guided 5-tab interactive Shiny studio (`run_dsemr()`).

## Continuous-time DSEM for irregular observation intervals

When intensive longitudinal assessments arrive at continuous, unequal elapsed
intervals $\Delta t_{ik} = t_{ik} - t_{i,k-1} > 0$, `dsem_ct()` estimates the
Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift matrix $A$ and diffusion covariance $Q = G G^\top$
directly via exact Padé `[6/6]` matrix exponentials $\exp(A \Delta t_{ik})$ and
Kronecker continuous-time Lyapunov covariances (Oud & Jansen, 2000; Asparouhov
& Muthen, 2024):

```{r}
library(DSEMr)

set.seed(2026)
dt <- runif(79, 0.25, 2.0)
y <- numeric(80)
y[1] <- rnorm(1, 0.5, 0.8)
for (t in 2:80) {
  ph <- exp(-0.65 * dt[t - 1])
  v <- 0.80 * (1 - ph^2) / (2 * 0.65)
  y[t] <- 0.5 + ph * (y[t - 1] - 0.5) + rnorm(1, 0, sqrt(v))
}
ct_dat <- data.frame(time = c(0, cumsum(dt)), y = y)

fit_ct <- dsem_ct("y ~ lag(y, 1)", ct_dat, chains = 2, iter = 300, warmup = 150, seed = 42)
summary(fit_ct)
```

Continuous-time impulse response curves follow $\exp(A h) B_0$ over continuous
horizon $h$:

```{r}
irf_ct <- dsem_irf(fit_ct, horizon = 6)
head(irf_ct$data)
```

## Random residual covariances and ARMA(1,1)

In bivariate two-level DSEM, individual differences in contemporaneous residual
co-fluctuation are modeled with a shared within-level shock factor (`logvf | y1 ~~ y2`
in extended `lavaan` syntax or `f BY y1@1 y2@1; logvf | f;` in section-based
syntax):

```{r}
sp_cov <- dsem_spec(
  outcomes = c("y1", "y2"),
  id = "subject",
  time = "time",
  level_type = "twolevel",
  random_slopes = TRUE,
  random_logv = TRUE,
  random_residual_cov = TRUE
)
cat(dsem_to_lavaan(sp_cov))
```

Moving-average residual dynamics (`ARMA(1,1)`) are estimated with an exact
$O(T)$ collapsed Toeplitz tridiagonal Cholesky sampler and a joint
$(s, \theta, \log \sigma_e^2)$ ridge move, returning a scale-invariant marginal
DIC.

## Launching the interactive Shiny studio

`DSEMr` ships with a 5-tab `bslib` interactive studio covering data exploration
and `TINTERVAL` grid preview, guided and syntax-based model building with live
SVG path diagrams and LaTeX equations, Rust-accelerated MCMC estimation and
diagnostics, post-estimation analytics (`STDYX`, Bayesian $R^2$, partial
correlations, hypothesis and Wald tests, IRFs, cluster rankings, DIC
comparison), and Quarto/R reproducibility bundle downloads:

```r
# Requires optional suggested packages: shiny, bslib, ggplot2
DSEMr::run_dsemr()
```
